claims.text: Conventional corrosion-resistant steels used in chemical-processing or nuclear-power applications typically have a homogeneous distribution of chromium and molybdenum.
A tailored annealing treatment can induce chromium short-range ordering in the target steels.
A tailored annealing treatment can produce nanoscale Cr-rich clusters in the target steels.
Standard homogenization minimizes short-range ordering and nanocluster formation relative to the tailored treatment.
Nanoscale Cr-rich clusters and local chemical ordering act as templates for nucleation and growth of a chromium-oxide passive film.
Short-range ordering causes chromium to segregate into nanoclusters.
Short-range ordering may cause molybdenum to segregate into nanoclusters.
The resulting nanoclusters promote rapid formation of a uniform, compact, dense, and adherent passive oxide film in an oxidizing environment.
A compact passive film impedes corrosive-species or ion diffusion and thereby limits material degradation.
Ordering-treated steel will form a more uniform and robust passive oxide layer than composition-matched homogenized steel.
Ordering-treated steel will exhibit lower corrosion current density than the homogenized baseline under identical test conditions.
Ordering-treated steel will exhibit less material loss than the homogenized baseline.
Potentiodynamic polarization in 3.5% NaCl can be used to compare corrosion behavior.
The proposed mechanism should apply to steels containing more than approximately 10–20 wt% chromium.
The proposed mechanism should apply in moderate- to high-temperature aqueous environments representative of chemical-processing or nuclear-power service.
The mechanism may not apply when the alloy composition or heat treatment does not permit detectable short-range ordering.
Ordering kinetics may vary among steel grades and cause variability in corrosion response.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in corrosion current density and improvement in passive-film morphology would falsify the proposed ordering-based protection mechanism.
